english: PAUL : « I asked around about Simon… »
Simon Collomb. The Angel of Death’s first victim.
PAUL : « Simon was seeing a shrink… nothing out of the ordinary. We see some not-so-nice things sometimes… »
PAUL : « Simon had kind of a strange childhood. »
PAUL : « Simon was raised in a very rigid, very Catholic family. Like, mass in Greek and all that. »
PAUL : « When… Tanguy died… I shouldn’t have been so distant.»
As you stare into your rearview mirror, you try to remember what Tanguy’s laugh sounded like…
The door opens and you see your old buddy Marco…
Marco… the one who stole your wife…
« No, Marco… »
Marco laughs nervously and it resonates off the cemetery walls.
You lean over. The flashlight illuminates the name of Zita Vellpeau, the third victim.
MARCO : « This is where her ashes are buried, along with the other members of the Moonie Tunes cult. »
You nod. The flashlight wavers and shines all around you for five seconds while Marco pouts.
You follow Marco through the stones. In the glow of his flashlight, you catch glimpses of portraits of unassuming faces that ignore you.
Once you get to the entrance, Marco turns his light off.
Marco appears.
Marco is a former taxi driver. A strange guy, a bit spacey and different. He’s been working at the stadium for a few years now.
That’s Marco. You like him.
The only noise in the room is the TV behind Marco. Before you came by, he was playing a soccer video game.
Marco drops his head between his shoulders. He starts to beg.
Marco sits up.
Marco looks away.
It’s an article on the Angel of Death and the actress Zita Vellpeau, the third victim.
One article goes over the life of Zita Vellpeau, the Angel of Death’s third victim.
It’s a sensationalist article about the third victim, Simon Gorodischer.
Documents about Ronan Besson, Charles Bougrain and Simon Gorodischer, the Judge’s first three victims.
You catch sight of Marco just sneaking inside.
You look over at Marco and head to his table.
You and Marco were old friends, until he… ‘stole’ your wife.
He’s shaking, his voice is low. He’s clearly uncomfortable. Marco’s a nervous type, but tonight… tonight it’s different.
You pay Marco’s tab and leave.
« Simon Collomb and Jules Lima? »
BARMAID : « They came in a lot. They were good clients, regulars… Simon didn’t drink, but he liked the atmosphere. »
BARMAID : « For… let’s say… a fifty… I’ll tell you who knew Jules and Simon particularly well. »
BARMAID : « For 250 euros, I’ll tell you who knew Jules and Simon… oh so very well. »
BARMAID : « 150 euros and I’ll tell you who knew Jules and Simon very well. »
BARMAID : « Apollonie Girardeau. A regular. She’s like a fixture here. She likes them young and I know she scored with Simon and Jules. »
BARMAID : « But she was too sketchy for him… She’s part of the Moonie Tunes. You know what that is? »
During a brief news story about the Angel of Death, you hear them mention the first victim, Simon Collomb’s family.
During an interview with a criminologist, the anchor refers to one of the Angel of Death’s victims, actress Zita Vellpeau.
You tune in right when Lady Monique is talking about the Angel of Death’s third victim, Zita Vellpeau.
Everyone knew — according to Lady Monique — that she was part of the Moonie Tunes cult.
The caller adds that she was Zita Vellpeau’s neighbor and on the night of her murder, she heard only female voices.
MYRTILLE: “One of my… girl pals told it to me. Have I ever mentioned Simone?”
MYRTILLE: “Simone was, well… like a sister.”
MYRTILLE: “Simone, she’s the one who got me into riddles. She did crossword puzzles, too. Stuff to improve your mind.”
MYRTILLE: “Anyhow, enough about Simone! You still haven’t answered the riddle…”
Suddenly, there’s a faraway look on her face. Perhaps she’s thinking about Simone?
